mentl/eeaf917:
collect_call_vectors was the relocation stamp's suggested first family
for the per-entry accumulator dual-run. Its walk expands emit-minted
nodes: the LShow arm calls collect_call_vectors_expr(show_node_of(h, x))
and show_node_of mints LCall(h, LGlobal(h, "int_to_str"), [x]) inside
wasm.mn. So part of the module's repr-vector set is created during the
emit walk and exists nowhere at lower time.

An accumulator fed at lower-time construction would miss every
interpolation's show call, and the wheel's own source is full of them, so
the set-equality gate would be RED by construction. Making it green means
feeding the accumulator from emit too, which is the relocation itself,
not a pre-landing.

collect_fold_tys is the viable first family instead: its LShow/LHash arms
accumulate the fold type and walk the operand, touching only nodes the
lowered tree already holds. The law the next family is tested against: a
module aggregation is dual-runnable only if every node it visits exists
before emit.

Docs only — no source change, no repin.

mentl/eec974c:
The general-multishot arc's first mechanism commit. world_tag_of_row's
sequence-sensitive FNV fold (a hash of hashes — cannot union, the semantics
refuter's kill of head-only composed worlds) is replaced by the OR-of-bits
projection: each effect name folds to one bit (its FNV-1a hash mod 32), a
row's tag is the OR of its names' bits, so tag(A u B) == i32_or(tag(A),
tag(B)) — a composed continuation's world is ONE i32.or at compose time,
and the future value gate is a subset test ((k & ~live) == 0 admits), which
IS the world-widening-resume semantics. A bit collision can only add a
phantom need — spurious refusal, never an unsound admit. Landed while the
field has zero readers.

The projection needs i32_or/i32_and/i32_shl: added as i32_xor's siblings on
the same substrate channel, all three homes (the memory.mn effect decl,
is_substrate_mem_op, the emit instruction projection).

mentl/ee2b679:
Pre-fix: $lower_pat for PLit (tag 132) loaded the LV-NODE pointer from
offset 4 of the pattern, then passed it directly to $lowpat_make_lplit
as the value field. LPLit's value field stored the heap-allocated LV
record's POINTER (e.g. 23889432 for LVInt(0)), not the actual scalar.

Emit's pat-match arm at emit_control.wat:456 calls $emit_i32_const on
$lowpat_lplit_value's return — emitting `(i32.const 23889432)` for what
should be `(i32.const 0)`. Surfaced when mentl2 tried to dispatch
list_index's `match tag { 0 => ..., 1 => ..., 3 => ..., 4 => ... }`:
all arms compared scrutinee against the LV-pointer values; ALL FAILED;
exhaustive-match fell through to (unreachable) trap. Trap chain reached
fn 1635 = list_index.

Fix per Lock #4 LowValue convention (mirrors $lower_lit_int's
$walk_const_payload_i32 at offset 4): extract the actual scalar from
the LV record at offset 4. LV tags 180/181/182 (LVInt/LVFloat/LVString)
all store scalar/str_ptr at offset 4. LVBool (183) handled above as
LPCon. Fallthrough emits 0.

Empirical:
  Pre-fix:  list_index `(i32.const 23889432)` × 4 arms; trap on first
            list_index call (parse_program → ... → list_index → match
            scrut against ptr, all fail, unreachable).
  Post-fix: list_index `(i32.const 0/1/3/4)` correctly per source. Trap
            depth advances to fn 522 (infer_program) → fn 523 (pre_register_
            fn_sigs) → fn 524 (pre_register_stmt) — wheel now executes
            full parse + reaches infer-stage pre-register walk.

Substrate dimensions:
  Graph?      $lowpat_lplit_value reads field 1 of the LPLit record;
              field 1 IS the OPAQUE-i32 scalar per LowValue convention.
              The graph's per-pattern scalar IS what emit reads.
  Handler?    OneShot — direct extraction at lower time.
  Verb?       |> sequential — read pat → load lit-node → tag-dispatch
              → extract scalar at offset 4.
  Row?        + Pure (lower is pure read).
  Ownership?  scrut_h carried; scalar valu
mentl/eebbc2b:
env_lookup and env_source now iterate by index instead of recursing
with slice(env, 1, len(env)). Each slice() created a new Vec — for
190 prelude bindings × hundreds of lookups, this was millions of
unnecessary copies. Index iteration is O(1) per step.

Also investigated and rejected:
- Lexer slice-at-end: string_slice is O(start_pos) due to UTF-8 scan,
  making it slower than str_cat + COW which is O(1) amortized.
- Import chunk-then-join: Lux's join uses fold + ++ internally,
  slower than direct ++ with COW for ~10 files.

Net: 13.5s → ~9.7s (28% faster) on hello.lux through self-hosted pipeline.

mentl/eecd123:
The gradient insight: no discrete levels. The compiler's power
scales continuously with annotations. Every annotation you add
unlocks guarantees — memoization, parallelization, real-time proofs.

ownership → refinements → native backend → gradient system →
synthesis → full self-hosting.

Each phase empowers the next in a virtuous cycle.

two-top/ee3097e:
The app aborts on the first tick of the second ggrs session in a process.
This was reported twice as "the app crashed after I tried to play a replay",
and the theater is not at fault.

bevy_ggrs resets RollbackFrameCount to 0 on any tick with no Session, which
is what makes the no-session Title screen sit at frame 0 for free. But
GgrsTimePlugin derives Time<GgrsTime> from that counter and advances it with
Time::advance_to, which asserts time never moves backwards. bevy_ggrs resets
the counter and not the clock, so they disagree:

  after match 1: rollback_frame=299 ggrs_elapsed=4.983333333s
  on the menu:   rollback_frame=0   ggrs_elapsed=4.983333333s

The next session then advances the clock to frame 0 while it still reads
4.98s, and bevy_time's assert kills the process.

Watching a tape is merely the most natural way to start a second session.
A second match crashes identically with no replay involved. Booting straight
into a tape is the one path that cannot fail, and it is how the theater got
tested, which is why this never reproduced on demand.

Reset the clock on the same condition bevy_ggrs resets the counter, rather
than hooking each teardown site, so the two cannot disagree no matter which
path drops the session: despawn_match, the netplay peer drop, or a forfeit.

theater::tests pins all three cases. The fresh-launch test earns its place
by passing while the other two failed, which is what located this. Also adds
step breadcrumbs through playback so a future theater fault names its step.

No sim behavior changes; SIM_VERSION is untouched. The sim reads Time<Real>
only, for interpolation, never the ggrs clock.

noodles/ee4c41c:
With every send off — the default, and most dice rolls — Freeverb's comb
bank and the feedback delay processed silence full-time, the priciest
always-on cost on a weak phone. A return with no open send now disconnects
from the duck bus, taking its whole subtree out of the rendered graph: it
wakes before a send gain opens and parks again six seconds after the last
send closes, past the tail. Offline renders make the same call statically.
Sound-neutral by construction and by receipt: dry master rms identical
(-5.1) across park/wake cycles, the wet melody stem gains +3.0 dB through
the woken path, and a dry master render runs ~10% faster — that share of
the audio thread comes back to the A16 whenever the room is dry.

The session track headers grow to clip height (min-height 62px, same as
.clip): the header is a tap target now — it opens the track's Sound page —
and fingers need clip-sized targets.
